summary: @onereach/phonenumber-interpreter preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: The package declares a `preinstall` script `node setup.mjs`. `setup.mjs` (itself obfuscated with `_0x`-hex identifiers and string-array indirection) downloads the Bun JavaScript runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/...zip`, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and uses `execFileSync` to run the tarball-shipped `math_init.js` under Bun on any `npm install`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB Bun-compiled CJS module (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) using obfuscator.io-style transforms: shuffled string array rotated via `push(shift())`, hex-mangled identifiers, and a mixed integer/char decoder table; static extraction of its strings surfaces `child_process` and `.aws` references. The package advertises itself as a libphonenumber wrapper and has no legitimate need for a second JavaScript runtime to execute a large obfuscated blob at install time. Corroborating smuggling signal: `package.json` declares `"files": ["lib", "index.js", "index.d.ts"]`, but the tarball also ships `setup.mjs` and `math_init.js` — the entire attack surface lives outside the declared files allowlist. Bun is used specifically because Node-oriented scanners do not follow into a Bun-executed sibling file, so the payload's actual behavior is hidden from most SCA tooling. The Bun runtime is fetched from its official project domain, but the harm is not the runtime fetch — it is the execution of an obfuscated, mismatched-purpose, undeclared payload shipped inside the tarball under that runtime.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
